clue.text: Baboon juvenile male breaks a great deal of equipment

explanation.walkthrough: 'Baboon juvenile male' reads as one creature, but the definition stops at 'Baboon'; the young male is separate wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The gelada is a grass-eating primate of the Ethiopian highlands, usually classed as a kind of baboon.

clue.text: Fine particle in sample lunar geologists picked up

explanation.surface: Scientists collect a tiny speck of moon rock from their sample.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' looks like the geologists' action, but in a down clue it tells you to read the hidden letters bottom to top.

clue.text: Mostly generous old Bond villain

explanation.walkthrough: LARGE without its last letter gives LARG, then O for old.
explanation.definitionFit: Emilio Largo is the eyepatched SPECTRE villain of Thunderball, an antagonist of James Bond.

clue.text: Blue duo fell out

parts.note: the letters as printed

explanation.definitionFit: Blue means sad or low in spirits, and doleful means mournful, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Mark learned about limiting inane gaming

explanation.definitionFit: The dagger (†) is a typographical symbol used to flag a footnote, so it is a printed mark.

clue.text: Certainly, 'name' boards first-class Arab sailing vessel

clue.text: Age-old British pastime is good, getting tougher without husband

clue.text: Scottish crime novelist joins European physicist

explanation.walkthrough: The novelist plus E gives another Scot, from a different century and field.
explanation.definitionFit: William Rankine was a nineteenth-century Scottish engineer and physicist, remembered for the Rankine temperature scale and cycle.

clue.text: Vigilante huntress stops violent gang rule

explanation.walkthrough: GANG RULE is rearranged into GUARNGEL and the goddess DIANA is put in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Guardian Angels are a volunteer street patrol group founded in New York, so a member is a self-appointed vigilante.

clue.text: Abandoning front, dash in retreat

explanation.surface: Troops give up the front line and run for it in a retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dash' and 'retreat' both look like running away; dash is the noun meaning style.
explanation.definitionFit: A lair is a hidden den or hideaway, a private place to withdraw to, which is a retreat.

clue.text: Washing articles abroad in middle of night

taken as written

parts.note: the central letter of the five

explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles abroad' asks for foreign words for 'the' and 'a': two from French and one from German.
explanation.definitionFit: To launder is to wash and iron clothes, so laundering is the act of washing them.

clue.text: Gust around summit almost causes delay

parts.note: a puff is a brief gust of wind

parts.note: the top of a mountain is its summit

explanation.walkthrough: The enumeration (3,3) points to a phrasal verb, which helps pin down the definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To put off something is to postpone it to a later time, a phrasal verb for delay.

clue.text: Raised extravagantly, bored by house in British colony once

extravagantly means wildly or without restraint, so these letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: the letters as printed
HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A child brought up in luxury, bored stiff at home in an old colony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bored' looks like ennui, but it means pierced, as with a drill.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodesia was the British-ruled territory in southern Africa that became Zimbabwe and Zambia, so a former colony.

clue.text: Disheartened indifferent US soldier with a nervous disorder

parts.note: neutral means taking no side, indifferent
GI is the familiar term for an American soldier
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dispirited, apathetic American soldier suffering from a nervous disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disheartened' looks like a mood, but it means losing the central letter; GI is the everyday name for an American soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Neuralgia is sharp pain along the course of a nerve, a medical condition of the nervous system.

clue.text: Repeatedly aiming at the sides, urine damaged volume-measuring apparatus

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
the sides of a word are its two ends, so only first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the ends of the word, taken twice because of 'repeatedly'
the letters as printed

explanation.surface: Someone keeps missing the pot and has wrecked some measuring equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: The ends of 'aiming' give AG, doubled to AGAG; with URINE these are rearranged to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rain gauge collects falling rain so the amount of precipitation can be read off, so it measures a volume.

clue.text: Square opening, partly round

parts.note: the middle stretch of the word

explanation.surface: A description of a square hole or window that is partly rounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square opening' reads as a shape; 'Square' alone is the definition, in the number sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine is three multiplied by itself, so it is a square number in arithmetic.

clue.text: Help to keep Rudolph's nose dry

parts.note: the first letter of the reindeer's name

explanation.surface: A plea for help keeping the red-nosed reindeer's famous nose from getting wet.
explanation.walkthrough: AID holds R. Rudolph is famous for his red nose, which makes the letter selection look like story detail.
explanation.definitionFit: Arid describes land or climate with very little rainfall, a direct synonym for dry.

clue.text: Tanks in a former Arabic union checked by, at the very least, Qatar, Iraq and Afghanistan

parts.note: taken as written

parts.note: first letter of the country
the United Arab Republic, the 1958 union of Egypt and Syria
first letter of the country
first letter of the country

explanation.surface: Military tanks in a defunct Arab alliance are inspected in three Middle Eastern war zones.
explanation.walkthrough: The Q interrupts A UAR, and the initials of Iraq and Afghanistan finish it. 'Tanks' suggests armour but means fish tanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquaria is the Latin plural of aquarium, the glass containers for keeping fish, which are also called tanks.

clue.text: University somehow gained odd bits of land without any agreement?

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university

parts.note: the letters as printed

indicators.note: the odd bits are the first, third and so on, so alternate letters are kept

parts.note: the first and third letters

explanation.walkthrough: U comes first; GAINED and the odd letters of 'land' are rearranged behind it. 'Agreement' sounds legal but means alignment.
explanation.definitionFit: Unaligned means not in line or not allied with any side, so in no alliance or accord; the question mark flags the stretch.

clue.text: Title changed on cover of boogie-woogie song

indicators.note: in a down entry, one thing on another sits above it, so the first piece comes first
changed means altered in form, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: the letters as printed

parts.note: first and last letters of the hyphenated word

explanation.surface: A song gets a new name when covered in a boogie-woogie style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover' is a music word that fits the surface perfectly, but here it means the outside letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Let It Be is the 1970 Beatles single and title track of their final album, a famous song.

clue.text: Edgbaston extremely happy to host new national team

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only first and last letters stay

indicators.note: a host takes a guest inside, so one piece holds another

parts.note: glad means happy
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Edgbaston, a Birmingham cricket ground, is delighted to stage a match for a new national side.
explanation.walkthrough: Edgbaston is a Test cricket ground in Birmingham, so the setting fits the answer perfectly while only its ends are used.
explanation.definitionFit: England fields a national side in cricket, football and rugby, which regularly plays Test matches at Edgbaston.

clue.text: One of two kings died charging English hill, not getting over

indicators.note: not getting something means going without it, so a letter is removed

explanation.walkthrough: E and D are followed by MOUND without its O. 'Over' looks like reaching the summit; it is the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Two Anglo-Saxon kings of England were called Edmund: Edmund I and Edmund II, known as Ironside.

clue.text: Bard finally enters piece to improve Kipling poem

parts.note: a piece is slang for a gun

the letters as printed
